items.title: How much does documented-decision coverage actually change onboarding time?
items.description: Jordan's team had only about 15% of its real architectural decisions written down anywhere findable — the rest lived in memory, old incident channels, or nowhere at all. Drag the coverage slider to see roughly how many productive days it takes a new hire like Jordan to stop hitting 'ask around' walls and start working independently. Coverage below ~20% barely helps; each undocumented decision still has to be rediscovered one near-miss at a time. Coverage never gets onboarding to zero — some context is always faster to just ask a person for.

params.name: docCoverage
params.label: Decisions documented and linked from the code

items.compute: const floor = 8; const base = 30; const onboardingDays = Math.round(floor + (base - floor) * Math.exp(-0.028 * params.docCoverage)); return { onboardingDays };

outputs.label: Days until a new hire works independently
